speaker: Joshua

comments.flawless: Joshua: The report was right on the first try. Bonus approved.
comments.done: Joshua: Case closed. Next time, check each word against the clues first.

all_clues_monologue: That's enough. An invoice nobody should open started a program nobody approved.
It turned the antivirus off and began to phone out. Time to press REPORT and write this up.

entries.title: Invoice 4471 with a zip file
entries.detail:
From: billing@acme-supp1y.com
To: Ben Nguyen
Time: 13:58
Attachment: invoice4471.zip

Your invoice 4471 is overdue. Open the attached file today to avoid a fee.
monologue: An invoice from "supp1y", with a number one where the L should be. And a zip file.
That's no real supplier. It's a real clue.
entries.summary: A fake invoice with a zip file, sent to Ben.

entries.title: Updates install tonight
entries.detail:
From: IT Team
To: All Staff
Time: yesterday 16:30

Tonight at 03:00 the laptops install their monthly updates. They may restart, and be a little slow in the morning.
monologue: A real note from IT, sent the day before. It explains a slow morning, but Ben's laptop got slow after lunch.
entries.summary: A real note about the 03:00 updates.

entries.title: Invoice 4470 from Pine Supplies
entries.detail:
From: billing@pine-supplies.com
To: Accounts
Time: 10:12
Attachment: invoice4470.pdf

Here is your invoice for last month. Thank you for your business.
monologue: A real supplier, the right address, and a PDF instead of a zip.
Compare it with the other invoice and the difference is easy to see.
entries.summary: A real invoice from a real supplier.

entries.title: "My laptop is slow"
entries.detail:
From: Ben Nguyen
To: IT Team
Time: 15:20

My laptop has been very slow since lunch, and strange windows keep popping up. Can someone look?
monologue: Ben's laptop got slow around lunch and he sees pop-ups.
Something is running on it. I need to find out what and when.
entries.summary: Ben says his laptop is slow and shows pop-ups.

entries.title: Friday lunch menu
entries.detail:
From: Facilities
To: All Staff
Time: 09:05

This Friday's lunch specials are soup and sandwiches.
monologue: Just the lunch menu. Nothing to do with Ben's laptop.

entries.title: Training day on Thursday
entries.detail:
From: HR
To: All Staff
Time: 11:40

Thursday is the yearly training day. Please book your session.
monologue: A reminder about a training day. Not related.

entries.title: Alert: odd sign-in stopped
entries.detail:
From: IT Alerts
To: IT Team
Time: 07:30

An alert fired for Anna Reyes' account yesterday night. IT already changed her password.
monologue: The alerts you turned on yesterday caught an old problem fast. Good. It's not about Ben's laptop, though.
entries.summary: An alert about the old sign-in, handled.

entries.title: Antivirus turned off
entries.detail:
Time: 14:05
Where: Ben's laptop
What happened: The antivirus was turned off.
Turned off by: UpdateHelper.exe, not by Ben

The antivirus is the program that looks for harmful programs. Ben did not touch it.
monologue: The antivirus on Ben's laptop was turned off at 14:05, and not by Ben. A program did it.
Something is hiding. That's a real clue.
entries.summary: The antivirus on Ben's laptop was turned off by a program.

entries.title: Updates installed
entries.detail:
Time: 03:00
Where: All laptops
What happened: The monthly updates were installed.
Result: It worked. Some laptops need a restart.

Updates close known holes in programs.
monologue: The monthly updates, just as IT said. A busy night, and a normal one.

entries.title: Pop-up blocked
entries.detail:
Time: 11:50
Where: Dana's laptop
What happened: The browser blocked an ad window.
Problems found: none

A pop-up is a window that opens by itself.
monologue: A pop-up, and the browser stopped it. A pop-up alone is only an annoying ad.
It's not a program running by itself, so it's not a clue.

entries.title: Scan found nothing
entries.detail:
Time: 12:30
Where: Carla's laptop
What happened: A virus check finished.
Problems found: none

A virus check looks for harmful programs.
monologue: A clean scan on Carla's laptop. Nothing to see.

entries.title: Old password tried again
entries.detail:
Time: 02:10
Where: Anna's account
What happened: Someone tried the old stolen password again.
Result: Stopped at the second step

The second step is the code on Anna's phone.
monologue: The old thief tried the stolen password again, and the second step stopped them. The upgrade you picked yesterday works.
entries.summary: The old stolen password was stopped at the second step.

entries.title: Old password tried again
entries.detail:
Time: 02:10
Where: Anna's account
What happened: Someone tried the old stolen password again.
Result: It worked until IT changed it

Without a second step, a stolen password is enough.
monologue: The old thief used the stolen password again, and it worked until IT changed it. That's old news, not today's problem.
entries.summary: The old stolen password worked once more.

computers.title: PROGRAMS > WHAT RUNS ON THE LAPTOPS

entries.title: UpdateHelper.exe
entries.detail:
Program: UpdateHelper.exe
Laptop: Ben's laptop
Made by: Unknown
Installed: today 14:03
List: Not on the approved list

The approved list names every program staff may run. IT did not install this one.
monologue: UpdateHelper.exe. It sounds like a helper, but IT never installed it and nobody knows who made it.
That's a real clue.
entries.summary: UpdateHelper.exe is on Ben's laptop and is not approved.

entries.title: DesignPro
entries.detail:
Program: DesignPro
Laptop: Dana's laptop
Made by: DesignPro Ltd
Installed: today 11:20, by IT
List: On the approved list
monologue: A brand new program, but IT installed it and it's on the approved list. New is not the same as dangerous.
entries.summary: A new program, approved and installed by IT.

entries.title: Office Suite

Laptop: Ben's laptop

monologue: Ben's usual office programs. Approved.

monologue: A normal program on Carla's laptop. Approved.

Computer: Backup computer
Made by: SafeCopy
Installed: last year
List: On the approved list
monologue: The backup program does its nightly job. Approved.

entries.detail:

Who: Ben
From: An email attachment
File: invoice4471.zip
Opened: 14:02

Ben saved the zip file from the invoice email and opened it a minute later.
monologue: Ben saved the zip at 14:01 and opened it at 14:02.
That connects the fake invoice to the minutes when everything changed.
entries.summary: Ben saved and opened the fake invoice's zip file.

A big download, but it is the update that IT announced.
monologue: 480 MB is a big download. But it's the approved update, at the hour IT said. Big is not the same as bad.
entries.summary: The big monthly update, as announced.

Where: Ben's laptop, in his user folder
What is happening: A hidden file keeps growing
File: sys32.tmp (now 3 MB)

It grows a little whenever Ben types.
monologue: A hidden file on Ben's laptop that grows when he types. It started right after UpdateHelper.exe.
Something is writing down what he does.
entries.summary: A hidden file on Ben's laptop keeps growing.

entries.title: Handbook opened

monologue: The staff handbook. Plain and ordinary.

entries.title: Ben's laptop calls an outside address
entries.detail:
Time: since 14:06
From: Ben's laptop
Sent to: An outside address (203.0.113.8)
How often: Every 60 seconds
Amount: about 2 KB each time

A normal program does not call a stranger on a steady beat, like a heartbeat.
monologue: Ben's laptop sends a small message to an outside address every single minute, since 14:06.
A steady beat means a program is phoning home. That's a clue.
entries.summary: Ben's laptop calls an outside address every minute.
